result.title: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
result.summary: AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people or other agents, purchasing services, exchanging information and delegating work. What an agent must respect is written in instructions, policies or agreements, but text alone cannot make it comply. It may make mistakes, be redirected by what it reads, or pursue different interests. For an economy of such agents to function, parties need agreements they can rely on without inspecting or trusting one another's agents. We introduce Proof-Carrying Contracts (PC2), a framework for making agreed constraints enforceable throughout an agent's interactions with a system. Before a requested operation can run, the agent must supply a machine-checkable proof that it preserves the agreed constraints in every case allowed by its model. An execution system called the Airlock checks the proof and controls access to the operation. The parties specify the conditions to preserve, while the agent supplies the reasoning needed to justify its decisions and remains free to adapt its strategy. This avoids having to design a separate permission policy and prove that every decision it permits is safe. We prove that the constraints hold at every instant during execution, even for an adversarial agent, and identify when this implies safety in the world. Reusable capability modules provide tools and guarantees from which contracts can be constructed. PC2 provides a foundation for an agent economy whose agreements protect both those delegating work and those carrying it out.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Proof-Carrying Contracts（PC2）框架：智能体在执行操作前须提交机器可检验的证明，表明其决策在模型允许的所有情况下都保持约定约束，由 Airlock 执行系统校验并控制访问。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作关注智能体行为的合约约束与形式化证明校验，不涉及视觉细节表征、latent 推理状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺乏可核查的具体联系。
